title: Concurrent caller hazard in advance_state_counter() private function
description:
What: advance_state_counter() (lines 445-461) reads and increments the state counter in two separate SQL statements. The doc comment states this is 'safe only for single-threaded use (Phase 1 constraint)' and mentions that Phase 2 must use UPDATE...RETURNING or hold a write-level transaction. However, the function is a private fn, not marked unsafe, and there is no compile-time guard against concurrent callers.

Why: A future maintainer may not read the doc comment when adding a call from a new async context (e.g., spawned tokio task). No test exists that simulates concurrent callers hitting this function. Phase 2 code paths could silently lose counter increments.

How to apply: (1) Add runtime guard that panics if called from concurrent context (via tokio::task::id() or a thread-local counter), or (2) rewrite to use SQLite UPDATE...RETURNING (available in rusqlite 0.30+) to make the read-write atomic. Document prominently.
